description:
Goal

A captured closure that is first published as a value and then invoked must return the same semantic result through interpreter, JIT, and AOT. First-class publication must not change the later call-result representation.

Signal

On base 636384f94 and during fz-k22.31 controls, a closure capturing n=40 is dbg-printed, then invoked with 2. Interpreter prints 42; JIT and AOT print a large tagged/reference word. The simpler captured-closure control that invokes without first publishing the closure returns 8 correctly on all paths.

Strategy

Minimize and pin the publication-before-call sequence. Trace the exact positioned CallableConstruction owner, wrapper selection, target private return layout, uniform public ValueRef return, and caller-local decode. Find the first boundary that returns or stores a reference word where the caller owns a scalar result. Repair that authority boundary; do not special-case dbg, infer from printed bits, or add a second return-shape selector. Evaluate after fz-k22.32 clarifies construction ownership, because both touch public wrapper authority.

Acceptance

Published-then-called captured closures, called-only captured closures, uncalled first-class references, opaque callables, and mixed direct/public controls agree semantically across interp/run/AOT. Full library tests and strict clippy pass; no temporary probes remain.
title: Preserve captured closure call results after first-class publication
